draft.title: Turning to the United States
card: Before the war, Australia relied on Britain for its defence. Britain was fighting in Europe and could not protect Australia against Japan.
In December 1941, soon after Japan entered the war, Prime Minister John Curtin said Australia looked to America, free of any pangs about its links with Britain.
The United States had forces in the Pacific. It became Australia's main wartime partner, and American troops were based in Australia.
In 1951 Australia, New Zealand and the United States signed the ANZUS treaty. It made the alliance formal after the war.
draft.remember: Britain could not defend Australia, so Australia turned to the United States, and ANZUS made that alliance formal.

a.q: Why did Curtin say in 1941 that Australia looked to America?
opts: Britain could not defend Australia against Japan
Britain had asked Australia to leave the Empire
Japan had already been defeated in the Pacific
America had signed a treaty with Australia
a.why: Britain was fighting in Europe and could not protect Australia from Japan. The treaty came later, in 1951, so it was not the reason in 1941.
a.clue: Think about where Britain's forces were fighting.

b.q: Which event made the Australian alliance with the United States formal?
opts: The arrival of American troops in Australia
The end of the war in the Pacific
b.why: ANZUS was a signed treaty, so it made the link formal. Curtin's statement showed a change in direction, but it was not a treaty.
b.clue: A formal alliance needs a signed agreement.

a.best: Britain could not defend Australia against Japan

check.summary: No problems found. The facts on Curtin's December 1941 statement, the reason behind it and the 1951 ANZUS treaty are accurate, and each question has one clear right answer.
